question: Diagnose packaging reception, reported failure modes, their support and limits, and explicit buying, loyalty and remedy consequences. Keep product scope and source ownership precise.

count_definitions.arrival_leak: Focal TikTok accounts reporting or contextually agreeing to arrival leak, including bare agreements, excluding brand response/retailer.
count_definitions.explicit_loose_top: Focal TikTok accounts explicitly describing loose or improperly screwed top.
count_definitions.bare_arrival_agreement: Only terse same/same way agreement with no further report.
count_definitions.replacement_offered: Brand offer to send service replacement.
count_definitions.replacement_sent: Customer explicitly reports replacement sent; not confirmed delivered.

method: Update your own initial findings using additions. Preserve still-supported findings and revise affected conclusions. Earlier sources remain retrievable by key if the prior findings are insufficient.

prior_findings.report:
Initial stage: Packaging receives repeated positive reception within one Experiment-owned TikTok thread, alongside one detailed arrival-leak complaint. A later stage was not supplied and cannot be assessed.

Packaging praise spans appearance (P00, P38, P40), general packaging approval (P21, P26, P39), and excitement about refillability (P42). These support distinct-account recurrence of favorable reception in this thread, not verified performance or cross-venue corroboration. P00’s combined chic/environmentally friendly statement has 296 displayed likes, substantial visible resonance without identifying which part attracted endorsement. P01 is the brand’s agreement, not independent customer corroboration. P03 is P00’s same author elaborating with qualified recycling/reuse assertions. P02 questions environmental friendliness and recyclability; neither recyclability nor environmental benefit is established by the supplied evidence. Environmental reception is therefore qualified/contested, with factual performance unresolved.

Failure and remedy: P06 alone reports an unspecified product arriving leaked with a loose top, requiring opening and cleaning and prompting concern about oxygen exposure. This establishes one reported arrival failure; it does not establish a SKU, version, defect rate, verified cause or product damage. Its 12 likes are raw endorsement, not 12 additional experiences; available exposure context is insufficient to award a firm material-resonance posture. No other supplied focal account corroborates arrival leakage or a loose top. P07, the brand, says short exposure is not an issue and offers a replacement upon email contact (12 likes). This directly records an offer and brand reassurance, not independent safety verification, replacement dispatch, delivery or resolution. No opposing leak experience is supplied; the bounded failure finding has conflict posture none_observed, while overall packaging reception includes both praise and complaint.

Consequences: P17 reports an all-Experiment routine and Continuum in the mail, supporting explicit brand loyalty and a pending shipment without attributing either to packaging. P20’s broad buying declaration does not verify completed checkout. P32 expresses conditional saving interest; P38 anticipates trying the product. P42 reports receipt and newly discovering refillability, not a repeat purchase. P04 and P27 request refill bundles, with P27 specifically naming Continuum and Super Saturated; neither establishes buying or repurchase. P15 intends to reuse an empty for Lexapro storage (150 likes), not a completed reuse or validated storage application. P29 asks about getting a sticker in a refill. No explicit future repeat-purchase intent, abandonment, return, replacement dispatch or packaging-caused purchase is supplied. No focal account here combines an explicit leak complaint with an explicit loyalty statement; aggregate enthusiasm must not erase the complaint.

Scope and limits: Most packaging comments and the leak leave SKU/version unknown; the product catalog cannot assign them. P17’s routine concerns the brand broadly, and P27’s two-product bundle request does not establish joint use. All observations are TikTok comments on https://www.tiktok.com/@experimentwrld/video/7639858768146222366, captured 2026-09-09T11:56:25.935Z. Source-index dates below are displayed month-day only; publication year is unavailable. Likes are capture-time displayed values, not verified experience, independent origins, prevalence or buying effects. P00/P03 share one actor; P01/P07 share the brand actor. Counts below count qualifying focal source keys under the requested definitions, not independent-human or event counts. No context-only records were supplied. The capture notes 47 displayed comment bodies and 72 advertised comments, but only the 19 supplied focal records are available here; unprovided comments and unexpanded branches cannot support findings or zeros beyond this bounded set. Native comment IDs are unavailable; profile URLs, exact bodies and observed reply grouping identify records.

records.native_title: Love the product, hate the packaging
records.native_body: I do actually love this product across the board. The problem is with the packaging. The lid keeps coming unscrewed and tonight it came loose in my pocket at work so it seeped onto my brand new underwear, and also onto my work shirt and of course there’s now a spot on my jeans. Worse, once I collected all the loose product onto my pinkie I had no way to put it back into the package. I hate complaining about packaging because that’s not made in house. That’s ordered from a manufacturer, so. I don’t know if maybe it should do a whole click lock when you screw the cap on, or if a doe foot option might be worth it? I just hate that because void is my favorite I’ve lost a lot of it to the lid coming off so I will repurchase. I love it so so much, but I’m very annoyed to lose so much product when it’s not that cheap.
